clue.text: National reps adjusted cost price (reduced) on charter

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y, so the shuffled letters follow the charter word

parts.note: a diploma is a document conferring a right or qualification, a kind of charter

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters of cost and the shortened price are rearranged
reduced tells us price loses a letter, here its final one

explanation.surface: Someone has fiddled the cost price of a national charter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the last letter of price, leaving PRIC; 'adjusted' rearranges that with the four letters of cost into TICCORPS. 'National reps' means a country's representatives abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplomatic body is the group of envoys representing their nations in a foreign capital.

clue.text: One way to fix bad credit?

definitions.text: One way to fix bad credit?

indicators.note: to fix here is to rearrange or doctor, so the letters of bad credit are reordered

explanation.surface: A tip on repairing a poor credit rating.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'fix' shuffles BAD CREDIT, and paying from your own bank balance avoids running up bad credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank card that draws straight from your account is one way of paying without borrowing.

clue.text: Champion for second time close to failure

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
a mo is a brief moment, a second

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone backs a champion for a second go after nearly failing.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to advocate or push it forward, a verb sense.

clue.text: Offers more than one penny, pre-decimal in ordinary words

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: in signals that the one-penny letters sit within the ordinary words

parts.note: verbs are doing words, a class of words
I is the Roman numeral one
D was the abbreviation for the old penny before British currency went decimal in 1971

explanation.surface: An auction bidder going one old penny higher, in plain language.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction, to bid above a rival is to tender a higher sum than theirs.

clue.text: Dismay as a neighbour of Santa turns up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: Santa is said to live in Lapland, whose native people are the Lapps

explanation.surface: Someone's dismay when a person from near Santa's home appears.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to horrify or shock them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Hardened criminal isn't seen casing area

indicators.note: casing means enclosing, so the shuffled letters wrap round the area letter
criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hardened criminal stays unseen while casing an area for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges ISNT SEEN into INSENSTE, which by 'casing' takes A in.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfeeling or callous; someone hardened has lost all sensitivity.

clue.text: Verbally stop item written by 10

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so a word that sounds like the synonym for stop is needed

parts.note: to check is to halt or stop

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop something written by someone else, voiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SPENDER, the answer at 10 across: a spender writes out payment slips.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank payment slip is filled in and signed by the person paying money out.

clue.text: Danger signal featuring after 6 at Monza?

definitions.meaning: a red pennant warns of danger, as on a beach or a racetrack
placed after the answer to 6 down it makes the chequered banner waved at the finish of a Formula One race such as the Italian Grand Prix at Monza

explanation.surface: A warning seen at an Italian motor race after a certain time.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like an hour; it is the answer at 6 down, CHEQUE, which with this answer forms CHEQUERED FLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarlet banner is a universal warning sign, and in motor racing it halts a race.

clue.text: Bad-tempered mare's last to leave, no doubt

indicators.note: to leave means a letter departs from the synonym for no doubt

parts.note: surely means certainly, without doubt

indicators.note: the last of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A grumpy mare is sure to be the last to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy and rude in manner; a surly person is ill-humoured.

clue.text: Slob in bar, knocking it back?

definitions.text: Slob in bar, knocking it back?

indicators.note: in places the slob word within the reversed bar
knocking back is sending backwards, so the bar word is reversed

parts.note: a pub is a bar
slob is an old word for mud or mire, which is ooze

explanation.surface: A slob at the bar downing drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slob' looks like a lazy person but is an old word for mud; 'knocking it back' turns the bar word round, giving BUP, and doubles as the drinking that defines the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking session where people knock back drink, like a slob sitting in a pub.

clue.text: Person responsible for laying out poet

definitions.meaning: laying out money is spending it, so this is one who pays out
Stephen ... was an English poet of the 1930s generation

explanation.surface: An undertaker who lays out bodies is also a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laying out' suggests laying out a corpse or a page, but it means paying out money.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is someone who pays money out; the other is the English poet Stephen Spender.

clue.text: Cardinal rejecting anything northern

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the dialect word is read backwards

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: A churchman of high rank refusing anything from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman; here it means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, of which this is the second.

clue.text: Line lost in presenting account to posh colleague with forked tongue?

indicators.note: lost means one letter goes missing from the billing word

parts.note: billing is presenting someone with an account or invoice
U stands for upper-class, hence posh
an ally is a partner or colleague

explanation.surface: A deceitful person sends a bill to a well-to-do colleague, losing a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with forked tongue' usually means deceitfully; the question mark signals the pun on a tongue split between two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked tongue jokingly suggests speech split two ways, i.e. in two languages.

clue.text: Harry O'Brien and a Scotsman

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Harry O'Brien alongside a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a first name for O'Brien, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Aberdeen, the city in north-east Scotland, is one particular kind of Scot.

clue.text: Annalist busy acquiring old papers

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the rearranged letters gain the old letter
busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A busy chronicler picks up old newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges ANNALIST into NATINALS, and 'acquiring' takes in O.
explanation.definitionFit: British newspapers sold across the whole country are called the nationals, as opposed to local papers.

clue.text: Old Bill nabbing revolutionary for one

indicators.note: nabbing means catching hold of, so the bill word holds the reversed letters

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a poster or bill

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: The police, the Old Bill, arresting a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police, but 'Old' is the definition and 'Bill' is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly; something or someone advanced in years.

clue.text: Stimulant — love it, second boxer admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the boxer goes inside

parts.note: to dig something is slang for loving it
Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for a stimulant, with a boxer let in second.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove drug acts as a heart stimulant, strengthening the heartbeat.

clue.text: Person wanting to keep piano up played again

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom
to keep means to hold inside, so piano goes within the wanting word

parts.note: a desirer is someone who wants
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Someone longing to keep the piano up plays a tune again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts P in DESIRER, making DESIPRER, and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated passage of music, so a reprised piece is one performed once more.

clue.text: Thoroughly weary butcher

definitions.meaning: to weary thoroughly is to exhaust, wear out
to butcher is to slaughter or kill

explanation.surface: A worn-out butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to exhaust someone and, informally, to murder them.

clue.text: Promissory note imbued with a delicate blue — whatever next?

indicators.note: imbued with means filled with, so the note takes in the colour

parts.note: an IOU is a note promising to pay
sky blue is a pale shade, so sky stands for a delicate blue

explanation.surface: A debt note coloured pale blue: what next?
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of exasperated disbelief at something outrageous.

clue.text: New blade flipped in deception's getting sharper

indicators.note: in places the flipped letters within the deception word

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick, a deception

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the new blade letters run backwards

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A new sword turned over in a con trick grows keener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' turns the new-blade letters round to EEPEN; the 's in deception's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming steeper, as a slope or rise grows more abrupt.

clue.text: Firm with policies making home safer?

parts.note: in means at home
surer means more secure, safer

explanation.surface: A company whose policies make your house safer.
explanation.definitionFit: A company issuing insurance policies is a firm with policies in the sense of contracts of cover.

clue.text: Pope's restricting abbey's latest provision for e-10

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the papal word holds the letter

parts.note: papal means belonging to the Pope

indicators.note: the latest letter is the last one

explanation.surface: A pope restricts the abbey's newest spending provision.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is SPENDER at 10 across, so e-10 is an online spender.
explanation.definitionFit: An online payment service is a facility provided for people who shop electronically.

clue.text: Means of paying bill a peer's pocketed

indicators.note: pocketed means held within, so the bill word holds a peer

parts.note: a poster is a bill stuck on a wall
a lord is a peer; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A peer pockets money meant to pay a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' suggests an invoice, tying with paying, but it is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A money order bought at a Post Office is a way to send payment.

clue.text: August men in provincial party rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards
in places the soldiers within the party letters

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, often called the Province
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers in a regional party marching upward in August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OR in DUP, giving DUORP, which 'rising' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means stately and dignified, close to lofty or grand.

clue.text: Italian lady introduced to London nanny

indicators.note: the answer is introduced to, lying within, the words London nanny

explanation.surface: An Italian woman meets a London nanny.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for woman, also a title for an Italian lady.

clue.text: Decline to fix number of games

definitions.meaning: the sun declines, going down below the horizon
to fix something is to fasten or establish it
in tennis a run of games makes up one section of a match

explanation.surface: Refusing to rig a certain number of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word covers the sun going down, fixing in place, and a group of tennis games.

clue.text: Pure Cockney politician reviewed top-class games venue

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: holy means pure, sacred
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at backwards, so the letters turn round

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A clean-living London politician reviews a smart games venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' turns AI (A1) into IA. Olympia, in ancient Greece, was the site of the original Olympic Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient sanctuary in Greece where the original Olympic contests were held.

clue.text: On boy's return, adult leaves test for a breather

indicators.note: return means coming back, so the boy word is read backwards

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so a letter goes from the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test
A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: When a son comes back, a grown-up quits an exam to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' makes NOS from SON; 'leaves' takes A out of TRIAL for TRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal opening is the passage through which one breathes.

clue.text: Inconsistent rules accepted during matches

indicators.note: during means within, so the accepted word sits inside the matches

parts.note: doubles are tennis matches between pairs
standard means normal, generally accepted

explanation.surface: Rules that change accepted practice during matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Principles applied differently to different people are a hypocritical, inconsistent code.
